hist-sa-01-c1.text: Joshua J. Mark (2020). Indus Valley Civilization. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-sa-01-c1.quote: The two best-known excavated cities of this culture are Harappa and Mohenjo-daro (located in modern-day Pakistan), both of which are thought to have once had populations of between 40,000-50,000 people
hist-sa-01-c1.claim: Its two best-known cities, Mohenjo-daro and Harappa, were each home to tens of thousands of people.

hist-sa-01-c1.text: World History Encyclopedia (World History Publishing). Indus Valley Civilization. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-sa-01-c1.quote: The Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro is believed to have been used for ritual purification rites
hist-sa-01-c1.claim: the Great Bath at Mohenjo-daro, a watertight tank possibly used for ritual bathing.

hist-sa-05-c1.text: Mark Cartwright (2022). Sepoy Mutiny. World History Encyclopedia.
hist-sa-05-c1.quote: The 1857-8 Sepoy Mutiny (aka Sepoy Rebellion, Indian Mutiny, The Uprising or First Indian War of Independence) was a failed rebellion against the rule of the British East India Company (EIC) in India.
hist-sa-05-c1.claim: The 1857 Indian Rebellion (also called the Sepoy Mutiny or India's First War of Independence) shook the system to its core.
